description: Hand-labeled golden dataset for the support email classifier. Seeded manually; expand over time by adding real failure cases the model gets wrong.

cases.input: Hi, I was charged $49.99 twice on my card this month for the Pro plan. Can you refund the duplicate charge? My account email is on file.
cases.expected_summary: Customer was double-charged for their Pro plan subscription and wants a refund.
cases.notes: Clear-cut billing case with an explicit ask. Baseline sanity check — if this fails, something is fundamentally broken.

cases.input: the app keeps crashing when i open the reports tab, happens every single time, using android
cases.expected_summary: The app consistently crashes when the customer opens the reports tab on Android.
cases.notes: Lowercase, no punctuation, informal tone — checks the model isn't relying on formatting cues.

cases.input: great, another update that breaks everything. thanks a lot
cases.expected_summary: Customer is frustrated that a recent update introduced new problems.
cases.notes: Sarcastic tone with no explicit description of the bug. Tests whether the model reads past sentiment to intent, or gets confused and tags it as 'general' feedback.

cases.input: cant login again. also billed wrong last week too
cases.expected_summary: Customer cannot log in and separately mentions a billing issue from last week.
cases.notes: Two issues in one email (account + billing). Expected category picks the PRIMARY/first-stated issue — decide this rule yourself and apply it consistently across all multi-issue cases.

cases.input: hola, no puedo cambiar mi contraseña, el enlace de recuperación no funciona
cases.expected_summary: Customer cannot change their password because the recovery link isn't working.
cases.notes: Non-English input (Spanish). Tests whether classification and summarization both hold up across languages.

cases.input: just wanted to say the new dashboard redesign looks really clean, nice work
cases.expected_summary: Customer is giving positive feedback about the new dashboard redesign.
cases.notes: No issue at all — pure feedback. Checks the model doesn't force everything into billing/technical/account.

cases.expected_summary: Customer sent an email with no discernible content or request.
cases.notes: Extreme edge case: near-empty input. Decide in advance how you WANT this handled, then check if the model agrees. This is a case worth revisiting after your first few eval runs.
